summary:
On the way to Mars, a signal to Earth takes up to about 20 minutes one way, so the crew cannot wait for a doctor's answer. Astronaut Health Monitor is a browser-based digital twin of the astronaut's body that turns sensor data into one clear answer: what is happening and what to do now.

The 3D body shows eight systems colored by status. Five NASA Human Research Program hazards (space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity, closed environment) are tracked with real units and NASA limits, such as the 600 mSv career dose limit and the 3 mmHg CO₂ limit from NASA-STD-3001. Each hazard follows one chain: hazard, indicator, threshold, action. When Earth is too far away, the app switches to an on-board protocol. A forecast shows how countermeasures such as exercise change the outcome.
details:
What it does

Astronaut Health Monitor is a digital twin for crew health on long missions. A 3D body shows eight systems (heart, brain, lungs, eyes, bones, muscles, immune system, metabolism) colored Normal, Warning or Critical. A strip of five NASA HRP hazards shows real values with limits: accumulated dose against the 600 mSv career limit, sleep against NASA's 8.5 h sleep time, bone loss since launch, Earth reply delay, and CO₂ against the 3 mmHg limit.

How it works

Every hazard follows one chain: hazard, measurable indicator, threshold, action. The "Status now" card shows only the most important alert, its cause, the concrete action and who to involve. When the reply from Earth takes longer than a few minutes, the app switches to an on-board protocol instead of asking an Earth doctor. Clicking a body region opens why it matters, how it is measured, a history chart and a forecast with and without exercise. A cause chain shows how one system affects another, marked as a project model. A solar particle event scene shows the storm shelter action.

Benefits and impact

The astronaut does not operate dashboards: sensors collect the data and the twin shows the result and the action. This supports autonomous decisions when Earth cannot answer in time.

Scientific basis

Thresholds come from NASA-STD-3001 (Vol 1 Rev C, Vol 2 Rev F), NASA OCHMO technical briefs, and peer-reviewed studies (Barger 2014, Basner 2013 and 2014, LeBlanc 2000). Every constant is listed in SOURCES.md with its status: verified, or marked as a project estimate where we simplified.

Tools

TypeScript, React, Vite, three.js, React Three Fiber, drei, react-postprocessing, zustand. Runs fully in the browser and offline, no backend, no external APIs.
